THE READING, WITH NO VERDICT ON IT.
(1) WHAT THE SERVED GRAPH NOW IS. One graph, two sources, one vintage line. The Nessie/Iceberg derive supplies the estate as before; the cloud stitch supplies what a repo-less runner cannot see -- 1,844 nodes and 723 inter-system edges folded, 27,423 duplicates skipped by co-key because they were already there. GOLD_SCRIPT went 0 -> 1380, S3_DATA_KEY 0 -> 294, API_ROUTE 86 -> 151. The line reads 'Built from the estate as of 2026-09-09 21:05:17 UTC. Stitch source: stitch-codebuild built 2026-09-09T19:55:00Z.' -- two ages, both stated, neither collapsed into the other. 1,771 of the folded nodes carry vocabulary=stitch-v1, so the interim population the CTO admitted is a query and not an archaeology exercise when S31 retires four of the five.
(2) WHAT THE FOLD DOES NOT GUARANTEE. Freshness. The fold verifies IDENTITY -- sha256 of the artifact against its own marker -- and never RECENCY. The stitch's age is the CodeBuild nightly's property (CG-s-23) and the marker's built_at is carried, not improved. Nothing here makes a stale stitch fresh, and nothing here hides one.
(3) THE NIGHT THE STITCH FAILS AND THE DERIVE RUNS. The fold is best-effort by the derive's own contract, so the derive commits with the stitch it can verify. If the producer failed, last night's two objects still verify against EACH OTHER, so the fold succeeds on a STALE stitch and the served line shows a day-old stitch_built_at beside a fresh Nessie vintage. That is the correct behaviour and precisely why the vintage is CARRIED rather than merged: a reader comparing the two ages is doing the right thing, and a reader who sees only one age is reading a line that predates this work. If the marker is unreadable, read_stitch_vintage returns nothing, the manifest carries no stitch keys and the sentence has no stitch clause -- an ABSENCE, never a default. The fixture asserts that absent case is byte-identical to the pre-CG-s-24 sentence.
(4) WHERE A SECOND COMPILE BUSINESS COULD RE-ENTER. Two doors. The local Kuzu of the stitch (kuzu_stitch_db / kuzu_stitch_load.py) is CG-s-26's to retire and was untouched here. The post-commit hook that republished stitch/ from either clone with producer=stitch-local is GONE from both (this laptop 19:46Z, site Z 19:58Z, rows S78/S81), so the cloud producer is the one writer -- and the marker read at this fold was stitch-codebuild, printed in the log line rather than asserted. The fold CARRIES the producer field and does not refuse on it (the issuer's ruling on S71), so if a hand-made stitch ever appears again the served line will say so instead of silently serving it.
(5) A THIRD DOOR, NAMED BECAUSE IT IS NEW. The five stitch-v1 types are a SECOND VOCABULARY for concepts the graph already types (GOLD_SCRIPT 1380 beside PipelineScript, S3_DATA_KEY 294 beside S3Key, PORTAL_COMPONENT beside Component, REACT_QUERY_KEY beside ReactQueryKey). That is admitted as a LABELLED INTERIM under R17 and is exactly why every admitted node is stamped. Until S31 unifies it at the producer, a reader who counts 'scripts' without deciding which vocabulary they mean will double-count, and the CVO's own C-S40 census gives the overlap numbers to do it correctly.
